description: On a runner with Docker and systemd: report mode changes nothing and shows the expected-containers list it would create; apply adds log rotation and build-cache limits to daemon.json without disturbing the keys already there, writes a file dockerd accepts, creates the list once, from every container present, marks it not reviewed, and never rewrites it, and installs an enabled prune timer whose script never touches volumes. Before the list is reviewed, a prune with no age limit removes no container and no image. After review, a stopped container that nothing protects is first recorded in /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal (0700 root directory, 0600 file) and left alone; a run inside the grace period leaves it and says until when; a run after it (the record moved back 145 hours) removes it and drops the record. Its age counts from when it stopped: one stopped 29 days ago and one never started, created 30 days ago, are recorded; one created 30 days ago that stopped just now is not (the times are set by stopping Docker and editing config.v2.json). A recorded container added to the list, or started again, loses its record. When the record cannot be written (a read-only bind mount), no container is removed and the exit is 1, through the timer's script and through Prune now; a GRACE_HOURS under 24 written by hand is refused by the prune; and when the review is withdrawn the prune removes nothing and clears the record. Stopped containers that are on the list, have an unless-stopped policy, or are labelled tc.keep are kept with their images. Images, with a test registry on 127.0.0.1 standing in for a real one: Dangling (and a settings file with no PRUNE_IMAGES) removes the untagged image only; All also removes the tagged image pushed to the registry, printing its repo@sha256 to the journal (and that reference pulls it back), keeps the one built here and says why, and keeps tc.keep; a failing docker image ls removes no image and exits 1. Which store the runner uses decides what All must do: on the classic image store as described; on the containerd image store, where every image has a digest, All keeps every tagged image and says why. The last steps restart Docker on the other store and check All there too, so both stores are covered whichever the runner starts with. The image is pushed to the test registry only on the classic store: on the containerd store it has a repo@sha256 digest without one, and that store's push used HTTPS on Docker 29.4.2 whatever insecure-registries said. With Docker restarted under extra daemon flags each time: a --log-driver=journald daemon and a --log-opt daemon get no log-opts in daemon.json and still start; a --log-driver=json-file daemon gets them and starts with them; a stopped daemon's flags are read from docker.service and its environment file, and flags it cannot resolve skip log rotation with exit 3; a daemon.json an earlier version already broke is reported as DAEMON WILL NOT START, exit 3, unchanged, and Docker really does fail to start with it. Bad input is refused with exit 2 before anything is written. Restarting Docker to load the new settings, and a host without Docker, are Tier 2. A container label is untrusted: one whose Compose project label carries a forged row cannot add a row or a field to the container listing, so a reviewed prune keeps the listed stopped container the forged row named, names the containers whose labels cannot be read, keeps them, and never prints the label; a new list leaves them off and says so. When docker ps fails but docker info answers (a shim on PATH), the prune prints ERROR, exits 1 and removes nothing, not even a network; Prune now exits 1; and the list is not created, exit 3. Writing daemon.json: the new file is made in the directory of the real target and renamed into place, so it keeps the mode, owner and group of the file it replaces (a 0600 file holding a fake proxy credential stays 0600 with its non-root group; a new file is 0644 root:root) and a symlinked daemon.json stays a symlink while its target changes and Docker restarts with it; a dangling symlink, or a link to a directory, is refused with exit 3 and nothing is created; after a successful Apply, a failed validation and Report mode, no .daemon.json.tc-* file is left in /etc/docker, and one left by a crashed earlier run is removed; Report mode on a host with no /etc/docker does not create it; seven changes in a row leave the newest five backups; and an immutable daemon.json makes the run exit 1 with the file byte-for-byte unchanged, no staging file and no backup.

steps.label: Container age: stopped 29 days ago; created 30 days ago and stopped just now; created 30 days ago and never started (Docker stopped and restarted to set the times); OLDER_THAN_HOURS=24
steps.run:
cat > /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-age <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-age NAME=CREATED[,FINISHED] ...: stop Docker, set those containers' Created
# (and State.FinishedAt) in their config.v2.json, start Docker again. Docker sets both
# times itself and has no way to change them, so this is how a test makes a container old.
set -e
declare -A ids
for a in "$@"; do ids[${a%%=*}]=$(docker inspect -f '{{.Id}}' "${a%%=*}"); done
root=$(docker info --format '{{.DockerRootDir}}')
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then systemctl stop docker.socket docker.service; else pkill -x dockerd; while pgrep -x dockerd >/dev/null; do sleep 1; done; fi
for a in "$@"; do
  n=${a%%=*}; v=${a#*=}; c=${v%%,*}; f="$root/containers/${ids[$n]}/config.v2.json"
  if [ "$v" != "$c" ]; then jq --arg c "$c" --arg f "${v#*,}" '.Created=$c | .State.FinishedAt=$f' "$f" > "$f.tc"
  else jq --arg c "$c" '.Created=$c' "$f" > "$f.tc"; fi
  mv "$f.tc" "$f"
done
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then systemctl start docker.service; else (setsid dockerd >/var/log/tc-test-dockerd.log 2>&1 </dev/null &); fi
for i in $(seq 30); do docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done
for a in "$@"; do docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} created {{.Created}}, finished {{.State.FinishedAt}}' "${a%%=*}"; done
EOF
chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-age
set -e
docker run --name tc-age-stopped tc-test-listed:1 /bin/true
docker create --name tc-age-fresh tc-test-listed:1 /bin/true >/dev/null
docker create --name tc-age-never tc-test-listed:1 /bin/sleep 3600 >/dev/null
tc-test-age tc-age-stopped=$(date -u -d '30 days ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ),$(date -u -d '29 days ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) tc-age-fresh=$(date -u -d '30 days ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) tc-age-never=$(date -u -d '30 days ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
docker start tc-age-fresh >/dev/null; sleep 2
docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} created {{.Created}}, finished {{.State.FinishedAt}} (stopped just now)' tc-age-fresh
sed -i 's/^OLDER_THAN_HOURS=.*/OLDER_THAN_HOURS=24/' /etc/default/tc-docker-prune; grep OLDER_THAN_HOURS /etc/default/tc-docker-prune

steps.label: Images: a test registry over HTTPS (a test CA, trusted by Docker and the system) at tc-registry.test, a name only this runner resolves to 127.0.0.1; five images no container uses: untagged; tagged for the registry and never pushed; pushed; pushed then deleted from the registry; tagged and labelled tc.keep
steps.run:
set -e
cat > /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-registry <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# tc-test-registry PORT DIR [CERT KEY]: a minimal image registry (the Docker
# Registry HTTP API v2, enough for docker push, docker pull and a manifest
# lookup) on 127.0.0.1, so a test can give an image a real registry digest
# without the internet. With CERT and KEY it serves HTTPS. Files in DIR change
# how it answers, so a test can switch them on and off:
#   htpasswd   "user:password": every request needs that Basic login
#   ratelimit  manifest requests get 429 Too Many Requests, as Docker Hub's do
#   delay      manifest requests wait this many seconds first
# Every manifest request is appended to DIR/requests.log.
import base64, hashlib, os, ssl, sys, time, uuid
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from urllib.parse import urlparse, parse_qs
PORT, DIR = int(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2]
for sub in ("blobs", "uploads", "manifests"):
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(DIR, sub), exist_ok=True)
def safe(s): return s.replace("/", "_").replace(":", "_")
def sha(b): return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
def flag(n):
    try: return open(os.path.join(DIR, n)).read().strip()
    except OSError: return None
class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def send(self, code, body=b"", headers=None):
        self.send_response(code)
        for k, v in (headers or {}).items(): self.send_header(k, v)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.send_header("Docker-Distribution-API-Version", "registry/2.0")
        self.end_headers()
        if self.command != "HEAD": self.wfile.write(body)
    def body(self):
        n = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
        if n: return self.rfile.read(n)
        if self.headers.get("Transfer-Encoding", "").lower() != "chunked": return b""
        out = b""
        while True:
            size = int(self.rfile.readline().strip().split(b";")[0], 16)
            if size == 0: self.rfile.readline(); return out
            out += self.rfile.read(size); self.rfile.readline()
    def route(self):
        u = urlparse(self.path); p = u.path; q = parse_qs(u.query)
        login = flag("htpasswd")
        if login:
            want = "Basic " + base64.b64encode(login.encode()).decode()
            if self.headers.get("Authorization") != want:
                self.body()
                return self.send(401, b'{"errors":[{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"authentication required"}]}',
                                 {"WWW-Authenticate": 'Basic realm="tc-test-registry"', "Content-Type": "application/json"})
        if p in ("/v2", "/v2/"): return self.send(200, b"{}")
        if "/blobs/uploads/" in p:
            name, rest = p[4:].split("/blobs/uploads/", 1)
            if self.command == "POST":
                uid = uuid.uuid4().hex
                open(f"{DIR}/uploads/{uid}", "wb").close()
                return self.send(202, headers={"Location": f"/v2/{name}/blobs/uploads/{uid}", "Range": "0-0", "Docker-Upload-UUID": uid})
            uid = rest.strip("/"); f = f"{DIR}/uploads/{uid}"
            with open(f, "ab") as fh: fh.write(self.body())
            if self.command == "PATCH":
                return self.send(202, headers={"Location": f"/v2/{name}/blobs/uploads/{uid}", "Range": f"0-{max(os.path.getsize(f) - 1, 0)}", "Docker-Upload-UUID": uid})
            d = q["digest"][0]
            if sha(open(f, "rb").read()) != d: return self.send(400, b'{"errors":[{"code":"DIGEST_INVALID"}]}')
            os.replace(f, f"{DIR}/blobs/{safe(d)}")
            return self.send(201, headers={"Location": f"/v2/{name}/blobs/{d}", "Docker-Content-Digest": d})
        if "/blobs/" in p:
            d = p.rsplit("/blobs/", 1)[1]; f = f"{DIR}/blobs/{safe(d)}"
            if not os.path.exists(f): return self.send(404, b'{"errors":[{"code":"BLOB_UNKNOWN"}]}')
            return self.send(200, open(f, "rb").read(), {"Docker-Content-Digest": d, "Content-Type": "application/octet-stream"})
        if "/manifests/" in p:
            name, ref = p[4:].rsplit("/manifests/", 1)
            if self.command == "PUT":
                data = self.body(); d = sha(data)
                for r in (ref, d):
                    open(f"{DIR}/manifests/{safe(name)}@{safe(r)}", "wb").write(data)
                    open(f"{DIR}/manifests/{safe(name)}@{safe(r)}.type", "w").write(self.headers.get("Content-Type", ""))
                return self.send(201, headers={"Location": f"/v2/{name}/manifests/{d}", "Docker-Content-Digest": d})
